arxiv-2111-06472.title: Direct observation of the radial magnetic field gradient in HD 58260 from spectropolarimetry of NLTE lines in emission Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2111-06472.creator: Marina Giarrusso
arxiv-2111-06472.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Marina Giarrusso. Because of the unquestionable presence of magnetic fields in stars, their role in the structure of stellar atmospheres has for a long time been a subject of speculation. In our contribution to this discussion we present spectropolarimetric evidence of the decrease of the radial component of the magnetic field with altitude in the atmosphere of HD 58260, a B-type magnetic star on the main sequence.

arxiv-2206-04077.title: Grand Color Axion
arxiv-2206-04077.description: Abstract We present a model that solves the strong CP problem via an axion parametrically heavier than the standard one. Within this picture the Standard Model quarks are embedded into a larger non-abelian Grand Color group that at high scales splits into ordinary QCD and an additional confining dynamics under which exotic chiral fermions are charged.

arxiv-2207-07569.title: Detectability of satellites around directly imaged exoplanets and brown dwarfs 2021 Detectability of satellites around directly imaged exoplanets and brown dwarfs – 5
arxiv-2207-07569.creator: Cecilia Lazzoni , Silvano Desidera , Raffaele Gratton , Alice Zurlo , Dino Mesa, Shrishmoy Ray
arxiv-2207-07569.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Cecilia Lazzoni , Silvano Desidera , Raffaele Gratton , Alice Zurlo , Dino Mesa, Shrishmoy Ray. Satellites around substellar companions are a heterogeneous class of objects with a variety of different formation histories. Focusing on potentially detectable satellites around exoplanets and brown dwarfs, we might expect to find objects belonging to two main populations: planet-like satellites similar to Titan or the Galileian Satellites - likely formed within the scope of core accretion; and binary-like objects, formed within different scenarios, such as disk instability.

arxiv-2211-11440.title: Kinetically stabilized inflation
arxiv-2211-11440.creator: Changhong Li, Hao Gong, and Yeuk-kwan Edna Cheung
arxiv-2211-11440.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Changhong Li, Hao Gong, and Yeuk-kwan Edna Cheung. In this work, we propose a string-inspired two fields inflation model to address the fine-tuning problem that the standard inflation model suffers. The fast-rolling tachyon 𝒯 \mathcal{T} originated from the D-brane and anti-D-brane pair annihilation locks the inflaton φ \varphi slowly rolling on a Higgs-like potential V ⁡ ( φ ) = − m φ 2 ​ φ 2 + λ ​ φ 4 V(\varphi)=-m_{\varphi}^{2}\varphi^{2}+\lambda\varphi^{4} and drives a kinetically stabilized (KS) inflation.

arxiv-2212-06825.title: Comment on “Harvesting information to control non-equilibrium states of active matter”
arxiv-2212-06825.creator: Antoine Bérut
arxiv-2212-06825.description: Abstract In the article Phys. Rev. E 106 , 054617 “Harvesting information to control non-equilibrium states of active matter”, the authors study the transition from one non-equilibrium steady-state (NESS) to another NESS by changing the correlated noise that is driving a Brownian particle held in an optical trap.

arxiv-2303-01373.title: Indirect reciprocity with stochastic rules
arxiv-2303-01373.creator: Yohsuke Murase
arxiv-2303-01373.description: Abstract Abstract Cooperation is a crucial aspect of social life, yet understanding the nature of cooperation and how it can be promoted is an ongoing challenge. One mechanism for cooperation is indirect reciprocity. According to this mechanism, individuals cooperate to maintain a good reputation. This idea is embodied in a set of social norms called the “leading eight”.

arxiv-2307-16805.title: Poincaré symmetries and representations in pseudo-Hermitian quantum field theory
arxiv-2307-16805.creator: Esra Sablevice, Peter Millington
arxiv-2307-16805.description: Abstract This paper explores quantum field theories with pseudo-Hermitian Hamiltonians, where P ​ T PT -symmetric Hamiltonians serve as a special case. In specific regimes, these pseudo-Hermitian Hamiltonians have real eigenspectra, orthogonal eigenstates, and unitary time evolution. So far, most pseudo-Hermitian quantum field theories have been constructed using analytic continuation or by adding non-Hermitian terms to otherwise Hermitian Hamiltonians.

arxiv-2404-19660.title: Decoder decomposition for the analysis of the latent space of nonlinear autoencoders with wind-tunnel experimental data
arxiv-2404-19660.creator: Yaxin Mo, Tullio Traverso, Luca Magri
arxiv-2404-19660.description: Abstract Turbulent flows are chaotic and multi-scale dynamical systems, which have large numbers of degrees of freedom. Turbulent flows, however, can be modelled with a smaller number of degrees of freedom when using the appropriate coordinate system, which is the goal of dimensionality reduction via nonlinear autoencoders. Autoencoders are expressive tools, but they are difficult to interpret.

arxiv-2508-09934.title: Efficient Volume Computation for SMT Formulas Thanks: A preliminary version of this work appears at the International Conference on Principles of Knowledge Representation and Reasoning (KR) 2025. The tool 𝗍𝗍𝖼 \textstyle\mathsf{ttc} is available at https://github.com/meelgroup/ttc .
arxiv-2508-09934.creator: Arijit Shaw, Uddalok Sarkar, Kuldeep S. Meel
arxiv-2508-09934.description: Abstract Satisfiability Modulo Theory (SMT) has recently emerged as a powerful tool for solving various automated reasoning problems across diverse domains. Unlike traditional satisfiability methods confined to Boolean variables, SMT can reason on real-life variables like bitvectors, integers, and reals. A natural extension in this context is to ask quantitative questions.

arxiv-2511-01293.title: Detecting Generated Images by Fitting Natural Image Distributions
arxiv-2511-01293.creator: Yonggang Zhang Jun Nie Xinmei Tian Mingming Gong Kun Zhang Bo Han
arxiv-2511-01293.description: Abstract The increasing realism of generated images has raised significant concerns about their potential misuse, necessitating robust detection methods. Current approaches mainly rely on training binary classifiers, which depend heavily on the quantity and quality of available generated images. In this work, we propose a novel framework that exploits geometric differences between the data manifolds of natural and generated images.

arxiv-2602-09908.description: Abstract It is shown that if F F denotes the number of filled cells in a superimposed pair of maximal orthogonal partial Latin squares of order n n , then F ≥ n 2 / 3 F\geq n^{2}/3 . This resolves a conjecture raised in an earlier paper by the current authors.

pmc-10533483.title: Vaccination of cattle with the Babesia bovis sexual-stage protein HAP2 abrogates parasite transmission by Rhipicephalus microplus ticks
pmc-10533483.creator: Marta G Silva, Reginaldo G Bastos, Jacob M Laughery, Heba F Alzan, Vignesh A Rathinasamy, Brian M Cooke, Carlos E Suarez
pmc-10533483.description: The apicomplexan parasite Babesia bovis is responsible for bovine babesiosis, a poorly controlled tick-borne disease of global impact. The widely conserved gametocyte protein HAPLESS2/GCS1 (HAP2) is uniquely expressed on the surface of B. bovis sexual stage parasites and is a candidate for transmission-blocking vaccines (TBV).

pmc-10656850.title: Association Between Occupational Stress and Sleep Quality: A Systematic Review
pmc-10656850.creator: Yongchun Mao, Gunasunderi Raju, Muhammad Azrul Zabidi
pmc-10656850.description: Occupational stress and sleep quality are prevalent issues that can impact the physical and mental well-being of adults. An association between occupational stress and sleep quality has been found. However, this association is not entirely the same across different occupational groups. Additionally, variations are present in the research design and instruments employed.

pmc-11475083.title: Efficacy of Radio Electric Asymmetric Conveyer Neuro Psycho Physical Optimization - Brain Wave Optimization-Gamma (REAC NPPO BWO-G) Treatment in Neurovegetative Dysfunction: A Case Report of Enhanced Cognitive Processing and Stress Resilience
pmc-11475083.creator: Valeria Modesto', Arianna Rinaldi, Vania Fontani, Salvatore Rinaldi
pmc-11475083.description: Neurovegetative dysfunction from chronic stress impairs cognition, emotional regulation, and quality of life, with limited relief from conventional therapies. The Radio Electric Asymmetric Conveyer (REAC) Neuro Psycho Physical Optimization - Brain Wave Optimization-Gamma (NPPO BWO-G) offers a novel non-invasive approach to restore autonomic balance through brain modulation.

pmc-11528169.title: Design, Implementation, and Analysis of an Assessment and Accreditation Model to Evaluate a Digital Competence Framework for Health Professionals: Mixed Methods Study
pmc-11528169.creator: Francesc Saigí-Rubió, Teresa Romeu, Eulàlia Hernández Encuentra, Montse Guitert, Erik Andrés, Elisenda Reixach
pmc-11528169.description: BackgroundAlthough digital health is essential for improving health care, its adoption remains slow due to the lack of literacy in this area. Therefore, it is crucial for health professionals to acquire digital skills and for a digital competence assessment and accreditation model to be implemented to make advances in this field.

pmc-11568781.title: What makes a good Samaritan: age, HLA matching, or both?
pmc-11568781.creator: Pietro Crivello
pmc-11568781.description: ection, along with other variables such as cytomegalovirus serostatus, donor/recipient sex matching, ABO compatibility, and more. The numerous variables affecting clinical outcomes, either increasing toxicity or improving protection from disease reoccurrence, present a challenge in understanding their interactions and the establishment of priorities to guide the selection of the best donor available.

pmc-11570454.title: hUC-MSCs mitigate atherosclerosis induced by a high-fat diet in ApoE−/− mice by regulating the intestinal microbiota
pmc-11570454.creator: Lin Yang, Bing Xia, Tianbao Qian, Jie Wang, Yuanhe Wang, Jialin Dai, Cuiyun Le, Xiaorong Yang, Jun Wu, Wenxin Wu, Jianwei Xu, Youbin Liu, Jiawen Wang
pmc-11570454.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe mechanism underlying human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hUC-MSCs) regulating the stability of atherosclerotic plaque was explored by establishing mice models of atherosclerosis induced by a high-fat diet and hUC-MSCs intervention.MethodsThe ApoE−/− mice atherosclerosis model was constructed using a high-fat diet, and mice were divided into a normal diet group (ND), high-fat diet group (HFD), hUC-MSCs treatment group (HFDM), while the blank control (BC) consisted of C57BL/6J mice.

pmc-11632112.title: Longitudinal serological and virological survey of hepatitis E virus in wild boar (Sus scrofa majori, Maremman wild boar) and fallow deer (Dama dama) populations in a protected area of Central Italy
pmc-11632112.creator: Luca De Sabato, Mariagiovanna Domanico, Paola De Santis, Daniele Cecca, Giulia Bonella, Giovanni Mastrandrea, Roberta Onorati, Luigi Sorbara, Bianca Maria Varcasia, Barbara Franzetti, Andrea Caprioli, Antonio Battisti, Fabio Ostanello, Ilaria Di Bartolo
pmc-11632112.description: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is recognized as an emerging zoonosis. Pigs and wild boars are considered the main reservoirs of zoonotic HEV-3 and HEV-4 genotypes. In Europe, autochthonous human cases of hepatitis E, mainly associated with HEV-3 and consumption of raw or undercooked pig and wild boar liver/meat, have increased over the last decades.

pmc-12432140.title: Sustainable Edamame production in an artificial light plant factory with improved yield and quality
pmc-12432140.creator: Tomoki Takano, Yu Wakabayashi, Soshi Wada, Toshio Sano, Saneyuki Kawabata, Wataru Yamori
pmc-12432140.description: A plant factory utilizing artificial light is an innovative agricultural model that enables efficient and sustainable crop production. However, its application to a diverse range of crops remains limited. Edamame, a highly nutritious legume, has gained global popularity, yet its long-term storage is challenging due to quality deterioration, restricting its market distribution to seasonal availability.

pmc-12500928.title: Rapid amyloid-β clearance and cognitive recovery through multivalent modulation of blood–brain barrier transport
pmc-12500928.creator: Junyang Chen, Pan Xiang, Aroa Duro-Castano, Huawei Cai, Bin Guo, Xiqin Liu, Yifan Yu, Su Lui, Kui Luo, Bowen Ke, Lorena Ruiz-Pérez, Qiyong Gong, Xiaohe Tian, Giuseppe Battaglia
pmc-12500928.description: The blood‒brain barrier (BBB) is a highly selective permeability barrier that safeguards the central nervous system (CNS) from potentially harmful substances while regulating the transport of essential molecules. Its dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a pivotal factor in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), contributing to the accumulation of amyloid-β (Aβ) plaques.

pmc-12809223.title: In vivo delivery of a fluorogenic antisense oligonucleotide into human leukocytes in a humanized mouse model system
pmc-12809223.creator: Nathan B. Seidel, Saurav S. Rout, Beverly Z. Packard, Kerry J. Lavender
pmc-12809223.description: Development of oligonucleotide-based therapeutics has been limited by the lack of effective in vivo delivery vehicles. We previously showed that the presence of an H-type excitonic dimer formed by the covalent binding of two fluorophores with significant transition dipoles on opposite ends of peptide or nucleic acid sequences of interest facilitated their delivery into live cells in vitro.

pmc-12815716.title: A pilot bedtime routine intervention for toddlers in primary care: variation by caregiver educational attainment
pmc-12815716.creator: Jodi A. Mindell, Joey Tsz Ying Lam, Zainab Salih, Megan Heere, Ariel A. Williamson
pmc-12815716.description: BackgroundA consistent bedtime routine (≥5 nights per week) is an empirically supported intervention associated with better sleep outcomes. However, few studies have examined the impacts of a bedtime routine on outcomes beyond sleep, and among families of lower educational attainment.

pmc-13068300.title: A Review on Medicinal Chemistry and Biological Activity of Dihydropyrimidinones Against HIV
pmc-13068300.creator: Debora I Leite, Fernando B Macedo, Murilo Marinho de C Lima, Isabelle S Brum, Jonathan Fragoso Miranda de Oliveira, Ana Clara S Costa, Stella C Duarte, Sarah Moon, Stefany de Castro B Moura, Andressa P de Oliveira, Nubia Boechat, Monica M Bastos
pmc-13068300.description: Dihydropyrimidinones (DHPMs), also referred to as pyrimidinones, are privileged structures widely employed in the search for new compounds capable of inhibiting HIV replication. This core is found in natural alkaloids isolated from marine sponge species, which are known to inhibit the binding of the viral surface protein gp120 to the CD4 receptor of target cells.

pmc-13336672.title: Stem Cell Differentiation Disperses Transcriptional Clusters via a Conserved Surface‐Condensate Trajectory
pmc-13336672.creator: Tim Klingberg, Irina Wachter, Agnieszka Pancholi, Matthias Akyel, Yomna Gohar, Priya Kumar, Ana Miguel Fernandes, Yuzhi Bao, Alica Schmidt‐Heydt, Marcel Piepers, Alicia Günthel, Marcel Sobucki, Elisa Kämmer, Süheyla Eroğlu‐Kayıkçı, Stephan Allgeier, Sylvia Erhardt, Vasily Zaburdaev, Carmelo Ferrai,
pmc-13336672.description: Stem cells exhibit exceptionally prominent transcriptional clusters, which dissolve with progressing differentiation. Although these clusters are assigned central roles in embryonic gene regulation, their formation and loss during differentiation remain poorly understood. This study reveals that these prominent clusters disperse along a conserved trajectory in mouse embryonic stem cells, fruit fly testes, and zebrafish embryos.

pmc-13542484.title: Stomatal cytokinesis defective2-dependent endocytic vesicular trafficking of abscisic acid
pmc-13542484.creator: Qian Lu, Yuanyue Shen, Aide Wang
pmc-13542484.description: SummaryAbscisic acid (ABA), a stressful phytohormone, is transported and signaled by clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) and clathrin-coated vesicles (CCVs). However, whether ABA promotes its cellular intake by CME and CCVs remains unknown. Here, this issue is first clarified by CME-mediated exogenous biotinylated ABA (bioABA) to localize in CCVs using three fluorescent macromolecules.

pmc-13681075.title: Vitamin B deficiency and sarcopenia: an integrated narrative review of metabolic, inflammatory, endoplasmic reticulum stress, and myokine signaling pathways
pmc-13681075.creator: Kisang Kwon, Sangmin Lee, Jenny Kwon, Seung Whan Kim
pmc-13681075.description: Sarcopenia is an age-related skeletal muscle disorder characterized by progressive decline in muscle mass, strength, and physical performance, leading to frailty, disability, falls, and increased mortality. Although its pathogenesis is multifactorial, growing evidence indicates that vitamin B complex deficiency contributes to muscle deterioration through interconnected metabolic and signaling pathways.
